messages:

To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-11T09:14:00Z
Subject: Discovery request — LexaHealth intake/triage use case

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the quick intro call offer. We're focused on improving intake triage for our digital clinic — routing and extracting structured fields (presenting complaint, urgency, meds, red flags) from short patient messages. Curious about Redwood's capabilities on structured extraction + function-calling for downstream workflows. Can we do a 30-min discovery today?

Attendees (LexaHealth): Alice Johnson (PM), Bob Chen (Engineering lead)

Best,
Alice

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Alice Johnson <alice@lexahealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-11T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery request — LexaHealth intake/triage use case

Alice — thanks, we can do 9:45 PT today. I'll invite Monica (CS lead) and Karthik (Applied ML / evals). Proposed agenda:
- Quick problem framing (10m)
- Current sample format & quality targets (5m)
- Model recommendations & structured-output approach (10m)
- Next steps and deliverables (5m)

Please share a small sample (50–200 rows) of deidentified messages ahead of the call if possible. Call invite sent.

— Aditya
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Alice Johnson <alice@lexahealth.com>, Bob Chen <bob@lexahealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-11T11:45:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap: model fit, evaluation plan, JSON-schema & tool-calling notes

Hi Alice / Bob — great to meet. Recap below plus concrete next steps. Internal copy for Monica / Karthik to take action.

1) Goal we heard
- Convert short patient messages into a fixed JSON payload (fields: complaint, severity, onset, meds_mentioned[], suggested_route) that our workflow engine can consume. LexaHealth target: >= 92% schema-valid outputs and >85% critical-field agreement for triage decisions.

2) Recommended models & config (initial)
- Candidate A: redwood-llama3-8b-q4 (good latency/cost balance, strong generalization)
- Candidate B: redwood-llama3-13b-q4 (higher accuracy on clinical phrasing; run as canary/expensive path)
- Runtime: enable function-calling (structured JSON) with strict schema enforcement + server-side validation fallback to lightweight reranking.

3) Eval plan & benchmarks
- We'll run three smoke runs over the sample:
  a) JSON-schema validity rate (is output parseable & fields present)
  b) Field-level accuracy (exact match / normalized match for enumerated fields)
  c) End-to-end triage agreement (binary urgent/non-urgent) vs your human labels
- Metric thresholds and acceptance criteria captured in attached eval_run_template.xlsx.
- Links: HubSpot deal + shared Drive with prompt/eval artifacts: https://redwood.app/hubspot/DEAL-9182 | https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1a2b3cLexa-EvalPack

4) Prompt sets & schema examples (attached)
- Attached: prompt_sets_v1.csv with prompt templates and edge-case probes; schema_examples.json with canonical JSON shapes and optional fields. We'll use a combination of constrained output prompts and post-output validator.

5) Tool/function-calling & retries
- Plan: function-calling for structured payloads; Redwood runtime will enforce response sizes and attempt 1 automated retry on schema-invalid responses with exponential backoff (200ms -> 600ms) and an alternate prompt that adds stricter instructions.
- If both attempts fail, route to a lightweight heuristic parser + queue for human review (we'll provide estimated fallback latency).

6) Quality/regression concerns
- Risk: clinical shorthand and negations causing attribute flips ("no fever" -> fever:true). We'll include negation-specific probes in evals and request clinician-labeled examples for high-risk edge cases.

7) Data & compliance asks
- Please provide a de-identified sample (150 rows preferred) and a short schema of downstream route IDs. If LexaHealth requires specific residency / SOC2 evidence, let us know — Monica will lead.

8) Owners & timeline
- Karthik: run model matrix + evals (deliver smoke report by 2026-10-18)
- Monica: security/compliance follow-up + SOC2 checklist
- Aditya: commercial SOW / timeline + pricing options (reserved can reduce per-token)

Next steps for LexaHealth
- Share sample dataset + confirm procurement contact (we think Bob Chen is the technical owner; please identify procurement/legal).
- Quick confirmation: are you OK with the two-model initial matrix?

Attachments referenced: [Attachment: prompt_sets_v1.csv (CSV, 38 KB)], [Attachment: schema_examples.json (JSON, 6 KB)], [Attachment: eval_run_template.xlsx (XLSX, 24 KB)]

— Aditya Rao
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Johnson <alice@lexahealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Bob Chen <bob@lexahealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T12:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, evaluation plan, JSON-schema & tool-calling notes

Thanks — this is super clear. Bob and I reviewed the plan; Bob is adding procurement/legal (he's cc'd). Two quick notes:
- We can produce a 150-row deidentified sample by end of week (will include a small set of clinician labels for urgent flags).
- We need confirmation on data residency — all processing must be US-only for now. Is that supported with Redwood Private or Dedicated options?

Also curious on the retry policy: if a retry still fails schema validation, do you provide a versioned artifact of both outputs and the fallback heuristic output for auditing? We need an audit trail for downstream clinical decisions.

On procurement: who should we loop in from Redwood for SOW / preliminary T&Cs?

— Alice
Product Manager, LexaHealth

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Alice Johnson <alice@lexahealth.com>, Bob Chen <bob@lexahealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-12T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, evaluation plan, JSON-schema & tool-calling notes

Alice / Bob — quick answers:
- Data residency: yes — we support US-only processing via Dedicated or Private deployments. Monica will share the options and a short checklist by EOD.
- Audit trail: yes — Redwood retains the original model output, retry attempts, and normalized fallback outputs in the evaluation bundle. We'll surface those in the smoke report and can add fields for tracing (timestamp, model_version, attempt_id).
- Procurement: please loop in contracts@redwood.com for preliminary SOW. I'll draft a short SOW (scope: 2-week eval + smoke benchmarks, optional extension for canary) and share in the next 24 hours. Deal reference: DEAL-9182.

Karthik / Monica: can you confirm you have bandwidth to start the smoke runs once the 150 deidentified rows arrive? Karthik — please set up a small runner that exercises: candidate A baseline, candidate B canary, and the retry-with-stricter-prompt path.

Thanks — we'll follow up with the SOW & Monica's compliance checklist.

— Aditya
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
